title: Revive: High-touch Triage + Handoff Prep (Caleb R.)
content:
Context / objective:
- Quick prep for 1:1 with AE (Jules) and incoming CSM from AE handoff pipeline. The goal: agree a short, high-impact revival plan for a high-touch account (RetailCo) trending towards churn risk, then capture crisp next steps and owner commitments.

Why this matters:
- RetailCo is ~7% of predicted quarterly ARR for the region; product usage down 35% month-over-month, billing paused on 2 seats pending feature parity ask. Previous touch cadence slipped after AE left.

Background (notes pulled from account page / last QBR):
- Primary contact: Priyanka Shah (Head of AI), technical champion: Tomas Rivera (Staff ML Eng).
- Last successful deliverable: POC in Nov 2024; in Jan they reported model perf drift on batch reranks vs baseline.
- Open requests: prioritized feature request FR-239 (per-customer reranking weights), infra sizing question for peak events, and security KBA for private deployment.
- Recent slack thread: they posted latency spikes during holiday sale simulation. See linked_artifacts.

Top signals pointing to risk:
- Login frequency: 3 active users -> 1 active weekly.
- API token usage: down 62% vs baseline.
- Billing: 2 seats paused; finance tagged for review.
- Support ticket jitter: 6 tickets in past 45 days; 4 related to model output quality regressions.

First-order hypothesis for decline:
- Without FR-239 the model outputs are noisy for their reranking pipeline; this increased manual rework and reduced trust. Latency spikes during simulations amplified operational risk and convinced product owners to pause expansion.

Meeting agenda (30 min) -- keep tight:
- 0:00–0:02 quick check-in & meeting objective (me)
- 0:02–0:08 AE recap + what they promised in handoff notes (Jules)
- 0:08–0:14 Customer posture summary (me) + critical tickets overview (Miguel)
- 0:14–0:22 Agree on immediate triage + prioritized 2-week action list (all)
- 0:22–0:28 Who owns what + SLAs for each action (all)
- 0:28–0:30 Quick sync on messaging to Priyanka + confirm follow-up meeting cadence (me)

Prep reminders (notes to self):
- Bring perf numbers for Jan–Feb (token-level latency, error rate).
- Have screenshots of failing reranks and sample logs (anonymized).
- Draft the 48-hour quick-win plan (see below) so we can get buy-in live.
- Prepare 1-sentence fallback escalation if feature can't ship in 2 weeks (e.g., shared model weights + tuned prompt as interim).

48-hour quick-win plan (proposed) -- present as "we can do these this week":
1) Engineering: narrow the regression root-cause (run failing queries in a controlled experiment) — owner: Miguel — ETA: 48h
2) Product: scope a targeted config workaround (temp weight override) — owner: Jules — ETA: 48h
3) Support: open a high-priority ticket and set a dedicated escalation hook (notify SRE lead) — owner: me (Caleb) — ETA: 24h
4) Customer comms: send a short, empathetic note outlining the triage steps and expected updates cadence — owner: Jules (draft) / me (send) — ETA: 24h

Example send-to-customer draft (short):
"Hi Priyanka — Caleb from Redwood here. We heard your report about rerank drift and latency during the holiday sim. We’re standing up a focused triage this week with Engineering and Product; immediate steps are to run a controlled diagnostic, apply a temporary config tweak if needed, and keep you updated every 48 hours. Jules will share the first diagnostic by EOD tomorrow. Appreciate your patience — we’ll move fast.
— Caleb"

Follow-ups and ownership (capture during meeting):
- Miguel: run diagnostic + share failing query set (artifact: s3 link) — due: 2025-02-19
- Jules (AE): commit to FR priority assessment and draft product workaround options — due: 2025-02-19
- Caleb (me): create high-priority support ticket, tag SRE, and own customer comms cadence — due: 2025-02-18
- Asha: prepare a short ROI note for the customer sponsor (1 pager) to remind execs of value — due: 2025-02-21
- Tomas (customer): confirm internal test window & share peak traffic sim schedule — requested by 2025-02-20

Open questions to surface in meeting:
- Is FR-239 truly blocking key workflows or is a config toggle acceptable as interim?
- What timeline does customer expect to see demonstrable improvement (2 weeks vs 1 month)?
- Who on their side will accept a short-term workaround vs requiring full feature?

Risks & escalation plan (quick):
- Risk: product team rejects interim fix -> Escalation: prepare offer of limited blue-green run using dedicated capacity (Dedicated team) + cost estimate; contact channel: eng-leads@redwood
- Risk: customer loses trust -> Escalation: schedule exec sponsor call and share bi-weekly public metrics dashboard (limited view)

Note style / shorthand (for my 1:1 debrief after meeting):
- capture exact ask wording from Priyanka (verb: "we need parity on per-customer weights")
- timestamp sample logs and paste to ticket
- label any internal blocker that requires hardware or security sign-off

Quick checklist to finish before meeting:
- [ ] Attach diagnostic graphs to drive link (done)
- [ ] Confirm Jules joins at start time (pinged)
- [ ] Prepare 1-slide "what success looks like in 2 weeks" (boil down to three metrics)
- [ ] Draft PR for internal escalation channel if needed

Post-meeting capture template (fill in live then copy to Confluence):
- Meeting time: 
- Attendees: 
- Agreed 48h actions + owners: 
- Agreed 2-week plan: 
- Customer message sent (y/n) + timestamp: 
- Next cadence: 
- Blockers / risks: 

Unresolved thoughts (brain dump):
- Could we offer a temporary model remix (light quantization + tuned prompts) to reduce latency without touching FR-239? If yes, what's the expected quality delta? Need research input.
- If finance paused seats pending a demo, pull in sales-ops to propose a 30-day conditional resumption tied to NPS follow-up.

TL;DR for calendar invite (short blurb):
- "30m: Rapid triage + handoff alignment for RetailCo. Goal: agree immediate actions to stop churn momentum and commit owners for 48h and 2-week plan."

-- end of notes --

(keeping this in users as a working scratch — will push finalized playbook to Confluence after we validate with AE/CSM)
